## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anuvijjakassapaṭipatti* ("The Conduct of an Investigator" or "The short chapter on the resolution of conflicts") is the fourteenth chapter of the *Parivāra*, the closing analytical manual of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The text outlines the necessary qualities, conduct, and proper character of a monastic inquirer or investigator who follows the Vinaya in resolving disciplinary issues and conflicts. The chapter has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 DharmaNexus identifies 261 matching passages across 23 Pali works, demonstrating heavy reuse in Vinaya literature and commentaries, including extensive overlap with the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* (§1.1–4.2 matching §1017–1020), the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vattakkhandhaka* (*Khandhaka* 18), and the *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares significant material with multiple numerical divisions of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*—predominantly the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), *Aṭṭhakanipāta* (AN 8), *Ekādasakanipāta* (AN 11), and *Sattakanipāta* (AN 7)—as well as the *Visuddhimagga* and the *Padaṭṭhānahāravibhaṅga* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments generated by DharmaNexus also detect shared phrasing with the Sanskrit Sarvāstivāda *Dharmaskandha* as well as Tibetan Kanjur texts such as the *Ratnamegha-sūtra* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
